items.title: Turkey’s Erdogan Captures City His Party Never Won in Elections
items.author: Murat Oztaskin
items.content: <article>The mayor of Izmir joined President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s AK Party, handing it control of Turkey’s third-largest city and an opposition stronghold it’s never won in an election in more than 23 years in power.</article>

items.title: IMF Chief Warns Governments to Act Now on Record Debt
items.content: <article>International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva says governments must act urgently to address challenges from the energy shock, rising interest rates and record debt piles. Increased spending following the Covid-19 pandemic and the wars in Ukraine and Middle East have pushed some nations "out of the safe zone," Georgieva tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Why Ken Paxton’s Estranged Wife Is Making the Case for His Senate Campaign
items.author: Beth Reinhard and Lisa Lerer
items.content: <article>Angela Paxton is urging Texas voters to support Mr. Paxton’s Senate campaign, even as she is divorcing him and accusing him of adultery. She has political aspirations of her own.</article>

items.title: Beach in Guam: Supreme Court Considers if Military Can Explode Bombs in This Habitat
items.author: Abbie VanSickle and Hiroko Masuike
items.content: <article>The Supreme Court will hear arguments over whether the U.S. Air Force can keep destroying munitions on a beach in Guam, a practice it began in 1982.</article>

items.title: As Race Tightens, Republicans Resume Tepid Support For Max Miller in Ohio
items.author: Emily Davies and Tyler Pager
items.content: <article>The embattled congressman, accused of throwing scalding water at his ex-wife and breaking his daughter’s collarbone, rebuffed earlier Republican calls to drop out.</article>

items.title: EU Prepares Import Cap on Chinese Hybrid Cars to Balance Trade
items.author: Alberto Nardelli
items.content: <article>The European Union is preparing so-called safeguard measures that would limit imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles into the bloc in a bid to reduce the trade deficit.</article>

items.title: SpaceX Seeks $40B For Nvidia Chips; Iran Steps Up Hormuz Attacks
items.content:
<article>Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, Bloomberg understands that SpaceX is in talks to borrow $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips in what would be among the biggest-ever debt financings for the AI buildout.

Oil gained as traders weighed increased flows through the Strait of Hormuz against a pickup in Iranian attacks against vessels.

And the Dutch government plans to reduce its investment vehicle’s stake in ABN Amro from 20.7% to 10.5%. 

Today's guest: Marguerite Bérard, ABN Amro CEO.

Corrects graphic at 29;47 to clarify that guest was referring to SMEs. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Taiwan Claims Two Hong Kong Residents Involved in Spying on DPP Lawmaker
items.author: Yian Lee
items.content: <article>Taiwan prosecutors said two Hong Kong residents paid for the surveillance of a lawmaker and his family, and indicted four Taiwanese individuals in a case they described as transnational repression.</article>

items.title: Singapore Foreign Affairs Chief Touts Robust Asean Growth in 'Crazy World'
items.content: <article>Singapore Minister for Foreign Affairs Vivian Balakrishnan tells the Milken Summit Asia that Southeast Asian economies are defying a "crazy world" to post high growth. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Malaysia Sets Nov. 14 for Malacca Vote in New Test for Anwar
items.author: Ram Anand
items.content: <article>Malaysia will hold local elections in Malacca on Nov. 14 in what’s set to be a fresh test for Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s Pakatan Harapan coalition, following setbacks in two state polls earlier this year.</article>

items.title: Singapore Sees Region Thriving Amid ‘Breakdown’ of World Order
items.author: Philip J. Heijmans
items.content: <article>Singapore’s top diplomat touted what he called “a moment of great potential” for Southeast Asia, as economies expand rapidly on surging technology demand even as much of the world faces growing uncertainties.</article>

items.title: Indonesia VP Stays in Office as Court Dismisses Diploma Case
items.author: Chandra Asmara
items.content: <article>Indonesia’s Constitutional Court dismissed a bid to unseat Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka over his educational credentials, keeping former President Joko Widodo’s son in office even as the judges cast doubt on whether he met the requirements to run in 2024.</article>

items.title: Takeaways From the First Maine Senate Debate Between Susan Collins and Troy Jackson
items.author: Lisa Lerer, Tim Balk and Emily Davies
items.content: <article>Senator Susan Collins, one of the most vulnerable Republicans in the midterms, clashed with the Democratic challenger Troy Jackson over President Trump, ICE and more.</article>

items.title: Amid Midterm Crunch, Trump Advisers Took Time to Help Russia-Aligned Government
items.author: Kenneth P. Vogel
items.content: <article>James Blair and Chris LaCivita, who are leading the president’s congressional campaign operation, traveled to Republika Srpska to provide election advice.</article>

items.title: Justice Dept. Turns to Partisans and Conspiracists to Fill Depleted Ranks
items.author: Glenn Thrush
items.content: <article>The civil rights unit has recruited people whose questionable work histories and dearth of education and experience might have disqualified them in the past, former officials said.</article>

items.title: North Korea Warns South Not to Cross Border by Even ‘Millimeter’
items.author: Soo-Hyang Choi
items.content: <article>North Korea said it would not tolerate even a “millimeter” violation of its territory after South Korea conducted mine removal operations along the two countries’ heavily fortified border following an incident in which three South Korean soldiers were injured.</article>

items.title: US Forces in Okinawa Face Curfew After Marine’s Arrest
items.author: Sakura Murakami and Yoshiaki Nohara
items.content: <article>The US Forces in Okinawa paused operations for 48 hours starting at noon on Wednesday and imposed a month-long curfew on military personnel, following the arrest of a US Marine on suspicion of murdering a Japanese woman.</article>

items.title: Five Takeaways in New Book From Thom Tillis, Who Turned on Trump
items.author: Annie Karni
items.content: <article>In “How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents,” Senator Thom Tillis details his regrets about backing President Trump’s agenda.</article>

items.title: Trump on Suspected Russia Plague: In Very Deep Discussions
items.content: <article>"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Lauren French, Senate Majority PAC senior advisor, says the PAC is making spending decisions week by week after pulling out of North Carolina and is looking closely at races in Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi. Gen. Charles Wald, USAF Retired, says threats against US military bases are not unusual and says the departure of B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford is being depicted “a little bit out of context.” (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anwar Set to Boost Spending in 2027 Budget as Election Speculation Grows
items.author: Danial Azhar
items.content: <article>Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is expected to tackle rising living costs in potentially his government’s last budget before he calls national elections.</article>

items.title: How a Maryland Shipyard Turned Into a Squabble Between Trump and Wes Moore
items.author: Luke Broadwater
items.content: <article>President Trump traveled to Baltimore to announce a major investment that he said would create new jobs. Gov. Wes Moore of Maryland, a Democrat, says he deserves credit, too.</article>

items.title: In Iceland, Rubio Dodges a Diplomatic Flap Over a Trump Map
items.author: Michael Crowley
items.content: <article>President Trump had posted a map on his Truth Social account in September depicting Iceland as part of U.S. territory.</article>

items.title: Democrats Look Strong in Polls, Thanks to These Voter Groups
items.author: Ruth Igielnik
items.content: <article>Different blocs are moving left. They could swing key Senate races.</article>

items.title: Kosovo Averts Early Election as Lawmakers Back New President
items.author: Gresa Kraja
items.content: <article>Kosovo averted a snap election as political parties reached a last-minute agreement to limit the powers of a war crimes court and choose Justina Shiroka-Pula as president.</article>

items.title: Trump Does Not Plan to Reimburse Taxpayers for Promotional Ads
items.author: Shane Goldmacher and Maggie Haberman
items.content: <article>A day after the president said his super PAC would pay for the ads, which had drawn bipartisan backlash, officials said that he meant moving forward. A new taxpayer-funded ad aired Tuesday.</article>

items.title: Red Diesel Move Sows Confusion for Truck Stops, Fuel Sellers
items.author: Will Kubzansky, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Ari Natter
items.content: <article>US President Donald Trump’s order allowing truckers to burn diesel normally reserved for tractors and trawlers won’t do much to immediately lower fuel prices, analysts said.</article>

items.title: Badenoch Can’t Shake Truss Specter in Bid to Woo Business
items.author: Katherine Griffiths and Jacob Reid
items.content: <article>The Conservative Party arrived at its annual convention determined to reclaim the mantle of sound money. The message is starting to land with business, even if voters will need some convincing first.</article>

items.title: Wrongly Indicted Man Seeks Inquiry of Official Conduct in Reflecting Pool Case
items.author: Devlin Barrett
items.content: <article>Lawyers for the former Olympian David Hearn accused prosecutors of ignoring their own evidence to indict him and then providing “blatantly false” information about what they knew when.</article>

items.title: An Influential Voice in the Climate Debate Has Died at 66
items.author: Clay Risen
items.content: <article>Joe Romm was a prolific writer who never hesitated to take on climate change deniers and the fossil-fuel industry — or even ostensible allies.</article>

items.title: Ex-C.I.A. Officer Who Stashed Gold Bars Admits to Far Larger $145 Million Scam
items.author: Devlin Barrett
items.content: <article>A plea hearing revealed a far larger pattern of fraud against the government, while keeping some key secrets still hidden.</article>

items.title: What, Exactly, Did Trump Say About Iran Taking Out Los Angeles and San Diego?
items.author: Shawn McCreesh
items.content: <article>President Trump’s comments caused an uproar from members of both parties. A White House official said he was taken out of context.</article>

items.title: Iran Increases Tanker Attacks in Hormuz as Oil Shipments Near Prewar Levels
items.author: Alex Longley, Ruth Liao and Grant Smith
items.content: <article>Iran has increased the pace of attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, just as oil shipments through the world’s most important energy chokepoint approach prewar levels.</article>

items.title: Republicans are spending to aid Darline Graham as the South Carolina Senate race tightens.
items.author: Emily Davies
items.content: <article>Senator Darline Graham, Republican of South Carolina, during a Senate committee hearing on Capitol Hill last month.</article>

items.title: Short on Cash, Democrats Weigh Big Bets to Unseat Entrenched Republicans
items.author: Shane Goldmacher
items.content: <article>With less money than G.O.P., Democrats are torn over where to spend in the final weeks. The party is making its biggest move in years against one of G.O.P.’s biggest blue-district survivors.</article>

items.title: Top Super PAC for Senate Democrats Raises Record $151 Million in Third Quarter
items.author: Shane Goldmacher
items.content: <article>Democratic Senate candidates have generally out-raised Republicans, but are struggling to match outside spending from Trump-affiliated groups.</article>

items.title: Man Arrested in Connection With Incident at UK Air Base RAF Fairford
items.author: Megan Specia
items.content: <article>A 22-year-old from London was the seventh person to be arrested by the counterterrorism police investigating an incident at R.A.F. Fairford last month.</article>

items.title: Drone Maker Anduril Pushes Into Subs With Maryland Factory
items.author: Jen Judson and Courtney McBride
items.content: <article>Anduril Industries, known for building drones and autonomous aircraft, is investing $3.7 billion to build a massive new shipbuilding facility in Maryland, a move that will enhance the US Navy’s nuclear-powered submarine production.</article>

items.title: Midterms 2026: Susan Collins, Troy Jackson Clash Over Costs in Maine Race
items.author: Greg Ryan
items.content: <article>Nazi symbols, sexual assault allegations and months of internal Democratic conflict have churned through the US Senate race in Maine. Yet with the election four weeks away, it’s the explosion in housing costs and record-breaking heating bills that Mainers can’t stop talking about.</article>

items.title: Indian Opposition Leader Detained After Voter Roll Standoff
items.author: Rajesh Roy and Santosh Kumar
items.content: <article>Police in India’s capital, New Delhi, temporarily detained key opposition leader Rahul Gandhi to end an almost nine-hour standoff, during a protest seeking the resignation of the chief election official over a contentious revision of voter rolls.</article>
